text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Government planning to close two army brigades, but there will no layoffs, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said.
- One and five markka coins minted in 1964 to 1993 to be withdrawn to prevent confusion.
- High quality of Finnish animal transport has received international attention and Finnish know-how is now being marketed abroad. @
- Debate about nuclear power has been based on emotion rather than analysis and rationale, PM Lipponen says.
- Statistics Finland study shows there is a correlation between education and long life.
- Forest industry talks with forest owners about wood prices failed on Wednesday. UPM-Kymmene plans to continue purhases at current prices, Enso which wanted a discount still considering.
KAUPPALEHTI
- U.S. forest industry lobby blaims Finland for protective EU customs levied on paper imports from the U.S., says wants them abolished in one or two years. @
- London analysts favour idea of a merger of Enso and Austrian fine paper producer KNP Leykam -- owned by Dutch KNP BT. Rough estimates value KNP Leykam at about $1.4 billion or seven billion markka.

- The best adjustment to economic fluctuation in EMU is strong corporate and public finances but a fund for unemployment contributions could also be set up to workk as a buffer, says secret memo discussed in the government's economic council.
- Finnish brokerage Evli has set up an investment bank, led by Kai Karttunen from CS First Boston. @
- Imports of cheap used trucks from Europe have grown rapidly but the opportunity for arbitrage gains is diminishing as Finnish price level falls closer to European prices.
AAMULEHTI
- Russia does not deny eastern European countries' right to membership in NATO but demands a high price, says Sergei Karaganov, director of the Russian science academy in Helsinki.
- Representatives of 27 countries to take part in simulation of nuclear reactor accident to be held in Loviisa next month to learn about information flow in Finland and abroad in case of emergency. @
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish peace and human rights activists to visit Kurdish areas in Turkey on Thursday.
- Ministry of trade and industry has plans to restrict concentration and vertical integration on the electricity market to ensure competition.
DEMARI
- Presidents Boris Yeltsin's and Bill Clinton's summit in Helsinki next week will not affect Finland's security policy, PM Lipponen says.
